general: Far over the misty mountains cold, to dungeons deep and caverns old, a fellowship was forged in shadow and in starlight.
The road stretches ever onward, past the fields of mortal men, into the vast and ancient dark where legends are born.
Nine companions stood at the edge of the known world, and beyond them lay only fire, ruin, and the faint promise of dawn.
In the age before memory, when the world was young and the stars sang their first songs, great deeds were done and greater sorrows endured.
The banners of a hundred kingdoms had fallen, yet still the last defenders held the gate, unmoved as the mountains themselves.
Across the sundering seas and the peaks of ice, the name of that ancient land was spoken only in whispers and reverent awe.
Where kings have wept and warriors have knelt, there lies a power older than the roots of the mountains.
The chronicle of those days was written in fire and blood, and those who lived through them spoke little of what they had seen.
A great age has passed, and with it the last of those who carried the light of the elder days within their eyes.
The tale of that fellowship outlived every stone of the cities they passed through, every river they crossed, every grave they dug.
Heroes do not choose their hour; the hour chooses them, and in that choosing, ordinary souls are made extraordinary.
The stars wheeled overhead in their ancient patterns, indifferent to the struggles of those beneath them, yet somehow offering comfort all the same.
There is a courage that comes not from hope, but from the knowledge that some things are worth fighting for even when all hope is lost.
Let the record show that in the darkest hour, when all light seemed extinguished, a small and unlikely hand carried the flame forward.
The world breaks every so often, and it is the task of the brave to gather the shards and remake it into something worth living in.
gandalf: A wizard is never late, nor is he early; he arrives precisely when he means to, and his timing is rarely without purpose.
I have walked this earth for longer than the memory of your eldest ancestors, and still I find it full of wonder and sorrow in equal measure.
Do not be too eager to deal out death in judgment; even the very wise cannot see all ends, and mercy has a power that justice cannot match.
All we have to decide is what to do with the time that is given to us — no more, no less, and nothing else matters.
There are older and fouler things than orcs in the deep places of the world, things that have not stirred since the first age of darkness.
Many that live deserve death, and some that die deserve life; can you give it to them? Then do not be too eager to dispense with either.
I am a servant of the Secret Fire, wielder of the flame of Anor, and the dark fire will not avail you here.
The greatest power is not in the staff or the spell, but in the word spoken at the right moment to the right soul.
Keep it secret, keep it safe — for there are eyes in the shadow and ears in the stone, and the Enemy is patient beyond all reckoning.
Even the smallest person can change the course of the future, if only they are willing to carry the weight of that responsibility.
Fly, you fools! There are things in the dark that even I dare not face while burdened with your safety.
The counsel of Gandalf is not always pleasant to hear, but those who have heeded it rarely found themselves worse for the experience.
I was there at the beginning of this age, and I shall be here at its close, though the shape I wear may change many times before then.
aragorn: I am Aragorn son of Arathorn, and if by life or death I can protect you, I will. This is my oath and my inheritance.
There is always hope, even when reason abandons it — I have learned this in the wild, in the dark, in the long years of watching and waiting.
The men of the west will not yield while I yet stand, and I have not yet begun to show them what it means to stand firm.
I would have gone with Frodo to the end, into the very fires of Mordor, but my road lies in a different direction, no less dark.
There is no glory in war, only the cold arithmetic of survival and the long silence that follows the last sword stroke.
A king does not seek the throne; he grows into it through loss and hardship, and learns that the crown is a burden before it is an honor.
We do not choose our lineage, but we choose what we do with the blood and name we are given. That choice defines us utterly.
Let the dead march with us — they owe a debt to the living, and I will call it due before the sun sets over the White City.
My blade has known many names before this one, and it will know many more; but in this hour it is raised for you, for all of you.
Hold your ground, hold your ground! Sons of Gondor, of Rohan, my brothers — even the smallest victory over despair is worth ten against flesh.
I have seen the Enemy's eye, and I do not flinch from it; let him see mine in return and know that Isildur's heir has come to reclaim what is owed.
frodo: I will take the Ring, though I do not know the way, and I am afraid of what it will make of me before the journey is done.
The Shire feels very far away now, like something from a dream I had once and can no longer quite recall.
It is a strange fate that we should suffer so much fear and doubt over so small a thing — such a little thing.
I cannot do this alone, Sam, but I am not sure I can do it at all; yet here I am, still walking, still putting one foot forward.
The shadow grows heavier with every step, and I am less certain now of who I was before I took this burden upon myself.
I begin to understand why the Ring was not given to the wise or the powerful — it would have destroyed them more elegantly but no less completely.
There is something in me that wants to keep it, and that wanting frightens me more than any orc or wraith that has crossed my path.
I do not want to be a hero; I want to go home, to the smell of pipe-weed and old books and the sound of the water mill.
The road goes ever on, but I wonder sometimes if the hobbit who set out on it still walks within me, or if he was left behind somewhere on the way.
sam: It's like in the great stories, Mr. Frodo — the ones that really mattered, full of darkness and danger, and sometimes you didn't want to know the end.
I made a promise, and I don't intend to break it; a Gamgee's word is not a thing to be given lightly or taken back without good reason.
There is some good in this world, Mr. Frodo, and it is worth fighting for — even if you have forgotten it for a while and need reminding.
Potatoes! Boil 'em, mash 'em, stick 'em in a stew — there are some comforts that even Mordor cannot take from a hobbit with a good appetite.
Share the load, Mr. Frodo, share the load — that's what I'm here for, and I'll not hear another word about going on alone.
I can't carry it for you, but I can carry you! And so I shall, even if it breaks every bone in my body trying.
The Gaffer always said that growing things takes patience, and I suppose going on a quest does too, though he never mentioned the orcs.
legolas: A red sun rises — blood has been spilled this night, and my eyes see it clearly though yours cannot yet perceive the signs.
The trees speak of shadow and unease; they have stood here since before the first men walked this land and they remember what was before.
I have lived through the sacking of Doriath and the fall of Númenor; one more battle will not diminish my desire for peace.
My arrows have not missed their mark in five hundred years of practice, and I see no reason to alter that record today.
The age of the elves is ending and I feel it in each sunrise, a slow and beautiful diminishing that no lesser race can comprehend.
There is a beauty in this world that I grieve to leave, and a darkness in it that I am glad to help unmake before I go.
We elves do not fear death as men do; we fear fading, the long diminishment of what was once bright into something grey and forgotten.
gimli: Nobody tosses a dwarf! And nobody calls us faithless without tasting cold steel and the fury of the mountains behind it.
The mines of Moria were the greatest kingdom ever delved beneath stone, and I will not hear them spoken of with anything less than reverence.
I never thought I would die fighting side by side with an elf, but if I were to choose my last companion, I could not choose better.
Dwarf-doors are opened by dwarves alone, or by those they trust; and Gimli son of Glóin trusts this fellowship, every unlikely member of it.
A dwarf's grudge runs deep and long, yes — but so does our loyalty, and I have given mine freely and without reservation to this company.
The craft of my fathers is in every stone of this mountain; I know its grain and its strength as I know my own axe-handle.
Give me a cavern over the open sky any day — there is beauty underground that those who only know the sun can never imagine.
sauron: I am the Lord of the Rings, and I do not share power with any who would call themselves my equal or my master.
The nine were given rings of power, and those rings were given purpose, and that purpose was the binding of all free will to my own.
You cannot hide from the Eye that does not blink; it sees through darkness and through flame, through stone and through the very fibers of your resolve.
One Ring to rule them all — this was not mere ambition; it was the completion of a design older than the trees of Fangorn.
Every rebellion against me has ended in ash; every king who stood against my shadow has become a name carved on a crumbling stone.
Your world is made of hope and light — fragile things, easily extinguished, and I am patient enough to watch them gutter out.
Come to me, Ring-bearer; lay down your burden and I will give you rest, and power, and the long peace of surrender.
